facts.text: On September 17, 1862, Antietam became the bloodiest day in American history when about 23,000 soldiers were killed, wounded, or missing.
The Battle of Antietam ended the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia's first invasion into the North and prompted Lincoln to issue the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.
A 8.5‑mile driving tour and numerous hiking trails let visitors explore the Antietam battlefield at their own pace.
The historic Dunker Church was rebuilt on its original site, and several family farms used during the battle remain preserved.
Antietam Iron Furnace Site and Antietam Village were listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.
The Antietam National Battlefield’s Visitor Center is a great starting point, and recent preservation work has opened up views across the center of the battlefield.
